answers.children: Dogue de Bordeaux are moderately good with children because their gentle demeanor with loved ones combines with exceptional loyalty to form patient guardians. The massive build and guardian history mean even a friendly nudge from this French Mastiff can knock a small child over, while their protective instincts make them watchful around family play. Their low energy suits calm indoor time rather than roughhousing. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 6/10)
answers.other-pets: Dogue de Bordeaux get along with other pets only with early introductions because their protective nature and wariness of strangers extend to unfamiliar animals. The breed's guardian background creates same-sex tension and low sociability scores, so a 100-pound French Mastiff may tolerate household pets yet remain aloof or dominant toward newcomers.
answers.exercise: Dogue de Bordeaux need 20 to 30 minutes of gentle daily exercise split into short walks because their massive build and low energy level lead to overheating and reluctance on longer outings. When unmet they become bored couch potatoes; light yard play suits this guardian breed far better than jogging or hikes.
answers.shedding: Yes — Dogue de Bordeaux shed moderately year-round because their short smooth coat releases hair that clings to furniture despite the lack of feathering or undercoat density. The smooth texture means loose hair is noticeable on clothing and floors in a home shared with this large guardian.
answers.hypoallergenic: No breed is truly hypoallergenic and Dogue de Bordeaux are not among those suggested for allergy sufferers because their short smooth coat still produces dander and moderate shedding. The French Mastiff's coat texture offers no special advantage for people sensitive to dog allergens.
answers.training: Dogue de Bordeaux are not easy to train because their stubborn nature and guardian background make them slow to respond and independent when they feel no immediate threat. The protective instincts that once served for estate guarding and cart pulling reduce biddability, demanding patient repetition from owners.
answers.lifespan: Dogue de Bordeaux live 5 to 8 years because their massive build and health robustness score of 3 reflect the significant health challenges inherent to the breed. This short range for a working guardian from France means owners must prepare for intensive care throughout the dog's adult life.
answers.size: Adult Dogue de Bordeaux stand 23 to 27 inches tall and weigh 99 to 150 pounds because their powerful Molossian-derived build gives them a massive head and heavy substance that fills a room. Living with this French Mastiff feels like sharing space with a silent 120-pound guardian whose mere presence commands respect.
answers.barking: Dogue de Bordeaux do not bark a lot because their protective temperament leads them to stay quiet until a genuine threat appears, relying instead on deep growls. Bred as estate guardians in France, these dogs conserve energy for watchful presence rather than frequent vocal alerts.
answers.apartment: Dogue de Bordeaux can live in an apartment because their low energy and calm indoor settling let them nap for hours provided daily short walks are given. The breed's quiet nature and minimal barking suit close quarters despite the 150-pound guardian size that requires careful navigation around furniture.
answers.first-time: Dogue de Bordeaux are not a good first dog because their stubbornness, protective wariness of strangers and significant health challenges demand experience and patience that novices often lack. The French Mastiff's loyalty is rewarding only for owners prepared to manage a massive, slow-to-train guardian.
